```{r, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE} library(tidyverse) library(ggpubr) data(mpg) ``` Every row in mpg is a car, every column a feature of that car. mpg stands for miles per gallon. ```{r} head(mpg) ```
## Basics of bar charts These uses the geom_col() function to display values *in* the data, geom_bar() to count the cases in a group. In this example, average highway miles per gallon (hwy) is displayed by a the type of car (class). ```{r} (hwy_class <- mpg %>% group_by(class) %>% summarise_at(vars(hwy), list(average_hwy= ~round(mean(.x), digits = 1)))) ```
### A basic bar chart That data is then fed to ggplot to produce a simple bar chart. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy)) ```
### A horizontal bar chart ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy)) + coord_flip() ```
## Amend fill colour
#### Standard gglot colours ```{r} plot <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, fill=class) + geom_col(width=0.5, colour = "black") + theme_minimal() plot ``` #### Other options ```{r} ggarrange( plot + scale_fill_grey() + theme(legend.position="none"), plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette="PuRd") + theme(legend.position="none"), plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette="Blues") + theme(legend.position="none"), ncol = 1, nrow = 3) ```
### Fill by another variable ```{r} (hwy_class_year <- mpg %>% group_by(class, year) %>% summarise_at(vars(hwy), list(average_hwy_year = ~round(mean(.x), 1)))) ```
The second variable is now the fill colour. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class_year, aes(x=class, y=average_hwy_year, fill=year)) + geom_col(width=0.5, colour="black") ```
The position argument (setting dodge2) moves the bars to appear alongside each other rather than stacked. ```{r} plot <- ggplot(data=hwy_class_year, aes(x=class, y=average_hwy_year, fill=year)) + geom_bar(stat="identity", position = "dodge2") plot ```
## Adding labels to data The geom_text function is what adds the labels: - had to move the aes() bit out of the geom_bar() bit to make this work.\ - the vjust bit moves it above and below the bar. A lower minus number would be higher above the bar. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy), vjust=-1) ```
Here the label is below the bar, vjust=1.5. The colour has been switched to white and the size increased also. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy), vjust=1.5, colour="white", size=6) ``` #### Adding them to our dodged plot above. We also have to 'dodge' the position of the labels within geom_text, again in the position argument. ```{r} plot + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy_year), vjust=1.6, color="white", position = position_dodge2(0.9), size=3.5) ```

## Other formatting
### Bar width Amend bar width within geom_col argument with 'width'. The default is 0.9, smaller values make bars smaller. Max = 1 and removes all space between bars. If you make the entire graph wider or narrower, the bar dimensions will scale proportionally. ```{r} more_space <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), width=0.9) less_space <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), width=0.5) ggarrange(more_space, less_space, ncol = 1) ```
### Change colours In the below the colour affects only the outline, without the fill the bars would be dark grey still. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), colour="blue", fill="white", width = 0.5) ```
Or bar colour can be changed by groups. - Add colour=var, where var is the variable you want to vary the colours by. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, colour=class) + geom_col(fill="white", width=0.5) ```
### Apply themes ```{r} p <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), fill="steelblue") p + theme_minimal() ```
## Select categories to show You can also select which items to show: ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, label=average_hwy)) + scale_x_discrete(limits=c("suv", "minivan", "pickup")) ```
## Alternative statistics
#### Barplot of counts Similar to a histogram, the stat="bin" command allows ggplot() to work like table(), but specifically for *numeric* values. ```{r} ggplot(data=mpg) + aes(x=cyl) + geom_bar(stat="bin") ```
Or with *character* values, try geom_bar without an argument. ```{r} ggplot(data=mpg) + aes(x=class) + geom_bar() ```

## Worked plots ```{r load_packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} library(haven) library(labelled) library(here) bsa <- readRDS(here::here("data", "synthetic_bsa_2017.rds")) # names(bsa) ```

### Bar chart for 1 way crossbreak (or for a frequency table) ```{r} (leftrigh <- bsa %>% mutate(dolefidl = as_factor(dolefidl), leftrigh = case_when(leftrigh == 9 ~ NA, TRUE ~ zap_labels(leftrigh))) %>% group_by(dolefidl) %>% summarise(leftrigh = mean(leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE), n = n())) ``` ```{r} dynamic_str_wrap <- function(text, plot_width = 7, num_labels = 1, char_width = 0.1, margin = 0.1) { max_label_width <- (plot_width * (1 - margin)) / num_labels max_chars <- max_label_width / char_width str_wrap(text, width = floor(max_chars)) } wrap_titles <- function(title, plot_width = 7, char_width = 0.09) { max_chars <- floor(plot_width / char_width) wrapped_title <- str_wrap(title, width = max_chars) return(wrapped_title) } num_labels <- length(levels(fct_drop(leftrigh$dolefidl))) x_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(leftrigh[1])]]) x_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(x_lab) y_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(leftrigh[2])]]) y_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(y_lab, plot_width = 5) title <- paste0(y_lab, " by ", x_lab) title_wrap <- wrap_titles(title) buffer <- mean(leftrigh$leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE) / 4 ylim <- c(0, ceiling(max(leftrigh$leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer)) (plot <- leftrigh %>% filter(!is.na(dolefidl)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = map_chr(as.character(dolefidl), dynamic_str_wrap, plot_width = 7, num_labels = num_labels, char_width = 0.08, margin = 0.1)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = factor(dolefidl, levels = unique(dolefidl))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = dolefidl, y = leftrigh)) + geom_col() + geom_text(aes(label = round(leftrigh, 1)), vjust = -1.5, size = 11, size.unit = "pt") + theme_gray() + labs(title = title_wrap, x = x_lab_wrap, y = y_lab_wrap) + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) + theme( plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1), text = element_text(size = 11), # This seems to have no effect??? plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10), size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10), size = 11) )) # Retrospectivly add colour plot + geom_col(fill = "#619CFF") # ggplot blue plot + geom_col(fill = "#7082d4") # natcen blue plot + geom_col(aes(fill = dolefidl)) + theme(legend.position = "none") plot + geom_col(aes(fill = dolefidl)) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ### Bar chart for 2 way crosstab - clustered ```{r} (leftrigh_sex <- bsa %>% mutate(dolefidl = as_factor(dolefidl), leftrigh = case_when(leftrigh == 9 ~ NA, TRUE ~ zap_labels(leftrigh)), sex = as_factor(Rsex)) %>% group_by(sex, dolefidl) %>% summarise(leftrigh = mean(leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE), n = n())) num_labels <- length(levels(fct_drop(leftrigh_sex$dolefidl))) x_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(leftrigh_sex[2])]]) x_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(x_lab) y_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(leftrigh_sex[3])]]) y_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(y_lab, plot_width = 5) title <- paste0(y_lab, " by ", x_lab) title_wrap <- wrap_titles(title) buffer <- mean(leftrigh_sex$leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE) / 4 ylim <- c(0, ceiling(max(leftrigh_sex$leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer)) (plot <- leftrigh_sex %>% filter(!is.na(dolefidl)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = map_chr(as.character(dolefidl), dynamic_str_wrap, plot_width = 7, num_labels = num_labels, char_width = 0.08, margin = 0.1)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = factor(dolefidl, levels = unique(dolefidl))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = dolefidl, y = leftrigh, fill = sex)) + geom_col(position = "dodge2") + geom_text(aes(label = round(leftrigh, 1)), position = position_dodge2(0.9), vjust = -1, size = 11, size.unit = "pt") + theme_gray() + labs(title = title_wrap, x = x_lab_wrap, y = y_lab_wrap) + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) + theme( plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1), text = element_text(size = 11), # This seems to have no effect??? plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10), size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10), size = 11), legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), legend.margin = unit(0.1, "cm") )) # Retrospectivly amend colour plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Accent") plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired") ```
### Drawing in NatCen colours ```{r} nc_colours <- data.frame( blue = c("#7082d4", "#8f99de", "#abb5e5", "#c7cced", "#e3e5f5"), pink = c("#f25c91", "#f57da8", "#f79ebf", "#fabfd4", "#fcdee8"), mint = c("#00ab85", "#33bd9e", "#66ccb5", "#99decf", "#ccede8"), purple = c("#b053a1", "#bf75b5", "#d199c7", "#debad9", "#f0deed"), orange = c("#ff8200", "#ff9c33", "#ffb566", "#ffcc99", "#ffe5cc")) nbl <- nc_colours[,1] # extract blue npi <- nc_colours[,2] nmg <- nc_colours[,3] npu <- nc_colours[,4] nor <- nc_colours[,5] nbl_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),1] # extract blue npi_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),2] nmg_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),3] npu_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),4] nor_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),5] nbl_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),1] # extract blue npi_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),2] nmg_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),3] npu_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),4] nor_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),5] ncl_5to1 <- unlist(c(as.vector(nc_colours[1,]), as.vector(nc_colours[2,]), as.vector(nc_colours[3,]), as.vector(nc_colours[4,]), as.vector(nc_colours[5,]))) %>% unname ncl_oppo2 <- nc_colours %>% slice(1,4) %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything()) %>% arrange(name) %>% select(-name) %>% as_vector() %>% unname ncl_seq3 <- nc_colours %>% slice(1,3,5) %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything()) %>% arrange(name) %>% select(-name) %>% as_vector() %>% unname # Two functions for diverging colours, Natcen... scale_fill_ga_diverging <- function(low_color = npi[1], medium_color = "white", high_color = nmg[1]) { scale_fill_gradient2(low = low_color, mid = medium_color, high = high_color) } scale_fill_ga_diverging <- function(low_color = nbl[1,5], medium_color = "white", high_color = nor[1,1]) { scale_fill_gradient2(low = low_color, mid = medium_color, high = high_color) } plot + scale_fill_manual(values = ncl_oppo2[7:8]) plot + scale_fill_manual(values = nbl) plot + scale_fill_manual(values = nbl_oppo2) plot + scale_fill_manual(values = ncl_5to1) ```
### Bar chart for 1 way crosstab - stack ```{r} dolefidl_x_leftrig2 <- bsa %>% mutate(dolefidl = as_factor(dolefidl), leftrig2 = as_factor(leftrig2), sex = as_factor(Rsex)) %>% count(leftrig2, dolefidl) %>% filter(!is.na(leftrig2) & !is.na(dolefidl)) %>% group_by(leftrig2) %>% mutate(p = 100*(n / sum(n)), psum = sum(p)) dolefidl_x_leftrig2 num_labels <- length(levels(fct_drop(dolefidl_x_leftrig2$leftrig2))) x_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(dolefidl_x_leftrig2[1])]]) x_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(x_lab) y_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(dolefidl_x_leftrig2[2])]]) y_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(y_lab, plot_width = 5) title <- paste0(y_lab, " by ", x_lab) title_wrap <- wrap_titles(title) ylim <- c(0, 100) dolefidl_x_leftrig2 %>% ggplot(aes(x = leftrig2, y = p, fill = dolefidl)) + geom_col() + coord_flip() (plot <- dolefidl_x_leftrig2 %>% group_by(leftrig2) %>% mutate(cum_value = cumsum(p), lab_pos = (cum_value - p / 2)) %>% # Without reverse of factor order, add 100 - before current formula mutate(leftrig2 = map_chr(as.character(leftrig2), dynamic_str_wrap, plot_width = 7, num_labels = num_labels, char_width = 0.08, margin = 0.1)) %>% mutate(leftrig2 = factor(leftrig2, levels = unique(leftrig2))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = leftrig2, y = p, fill = fct_rev(dolefidl))) + geom_col(position = "stack") + geom_text(aes(label = round(p,0), y = lab_pos), size = 11, size.unit = "pt") + # vjust = -1, coord_flip() + theme_gray() + labs(title = title_wrap, x = x_lab_wrap, y = y_lab_wrap) + theme( plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1), text = element_text(size = 11), # This seems to have no effect??? plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10), size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10), size = 11), legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), legend.margin = unit(0.1, "cm") )) plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Accent") plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") plot + scale_fill_manual(values = rev(c(nbl,"grey"))) plot + scale_fill_manual(values = rev(c(npu,"grey"))) plot + scale_fill_manual(values = rev(c(nmg,"grey"))) ```

### Exploration of **str_wrap** Takes a positive integer giving the target line width (in number of characters). A width less than or equal to 1 will put each word on its own line. ```{r} leftrigh %>% filter(!is.na(dolefidl)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = str_wrap(dolefidl, width = 16), y = leftrigh)) + geom_col() + labs(x = "dolefidl") # A standard ggplot is 7 inches wide. # An inch is 2.54cm library(grid) cats <- levels(fct_drop(leftrigh$dolefidl)) text_grob <- textGrob(cats[2], gp=gpar(fontfamily="Sans", fontsize=11)) width <- grobWidth(text_grob) height <- grobHeight(text_grob) width_cm <- convertWidth(width, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE) height_cm <- convertHeight(height, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE) cat_lengths <- map_dbl(cats, ~convertWidth(grobWidth(textGrob(.x, gp=gpar(fontfamily="Arial", fontsize=11))),"cm", valueOnly = TRUE)) names(cat_lengths) <- cats cat_lengths sum(cat_lengths) / 2.54 ```

## Functions
### A frequency bar chart Decide to use: age and where someone would go for advice, I can then use for a crosstab later as well. ```{r} bsa <- bsa %>% mutate(across(c(RAgecat5,hadvice), ~as_factor(.x)), hadvice2 = fct_collapse(hadvice, `Someone else` = c("Neighbour", "Someone I work with", "Someone else"))) bsa %>% count(hadvice2) bsa %>% count(RAgecat5) bsa %>% count(RAgecat5, hadvice) ```
**Step 1** will be to create a function to generate a table of data, to then plot. ```{r} (hadvice <- bsa %>% filter(!is.na(hadvice2)) %>% group_by(hadvice2) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>% mutate(p = 100 * (n / sum(n)))) hadvice$x_label <- var_label(bsa$hadvice2) hadvice freq <- function(dat, var) { x_var <- as.character(substitute(var)) table <- dat %>% filter(!is.na({{var}})) %>% group_by({{var}}) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>% mutate(p = 100 * (n / sum(n))) table$x_label <- var_label(dat[[x_var]]) return(table) } hadvice <- freq(dat = bsa, var = hadvice2) hadvice ```
**Step 2:** Decant that data into a ggplot of approved type ```{r} dynamic_str_wrap <- function(text, plot_width = 7, num_labels = 1, char_width = 0.1, margin = 0.1) { max_label_width <- (plot_width * (1 - margin)) / num_labels max_chars <- max_label_width / char_width str_wrap(text, width = floor(max_chars)) } wrap_titles <- function(title, plot_width = 7, char_width = 0.09) { max_chars <- floor(plot_width / char_width) wrapped_title <- str_wrap(title, width = max_chars) return(wrapped_title) } num_labels <- length(levels(fct_drop(hadvice$hadvice2))) x_lab <- unique(hadvice[,4]) x_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(x_lab) # y_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(hadvice[2])]]) # y_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(y_lab, plot_width = 5) title <- paste0(x_lab) title_wrap <- wrap_titles(title) buffer <- mean(hadvice$p, na.rm = TRUE) / 4 ylim <- c(0, ceiling(max(hadvice$p, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer)) (plot <- hadvice %>% filter(!is.na(hadvice2)) %>% mutate(hadvice2 = map_chr(as.character(hadvice2), dynamic_str_wrap, plot_width = 7, num_labels = num_labels, char_width = 0.08, margin = 0.1)) %>% mutate(hadvice2 = factor(hadvice2, levels = unique(hadvice2))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = hadvice2, y = p)) + geom_col() + geom_text(aes(label = round(p, 1)), vjust = -1.5, size = 11, size.unit = "pt") + theme_gray() + labs(title = title_wrap, x = NULL, y = "%" ) + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) + theme( plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1), text = element_text(size = 11), # This seems to have no effect??? plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5), axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10), size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10), size = 11) )) ``` \*\* Step 3:\*\* Decant that bar chart code into a function ```{r} bar <- function(dat, colour = NULL, palette = NULL) { # Define some potential custom palettes nbl <- nc_colours[,1] # extract blue npi <- nc_colours[,2] nmg <- nc_colours[,3] npu <- nc_colours[,4] nor <- nc_colours[,5] nbl_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),1] # extract blue npi_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),2] nmg_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),3] npu_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),4] nor_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),5] nbl_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),1] # extract blue npi_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),2] nmg_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),3] npu_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),4] nor_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),5] ncl_5to1 <- unlist(c(as.vector(nc_colours[1,]), as.vector(nc_colours[2,]), as.vector(nc_colours[3,]), as.vector(nc_colours[4,]), as.vector(nc_colours[5,]))) %>% unname ncl_oppo2 <- nc_colours %>% slice(1,4) %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything()) %>% arrange(name) %>% select(-name) %>% as_vector() %>% unname ncl_seq3 <- nc_colours %>% slice(1,3,5) %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything()) %>% arrange(name) %>% select(-name) %>% as_vector() %>% unname dynamic_str_wrap <- function(text, plot_width = 7, num_labels = 1, char_width = 0.1, margin = 0.1) { max_label_width <- (plot_width * (1 - margin)) / num_labels max_chars <- max_label_width / char_width str_wrap(text, width = floor(max_chars)) } wrap_titles <- function(title, plot_width = 7, char_width = 0.09) { max_chars <- floor(plot_width / char_width) wrapped_title <- str_wrap(title, width = max_chars) return(wrapped_title) } num_labels <- length(levels(fct_drop(hadvice[[1]]))) x_lab <- unique(dat[,4]) x_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(x_lab) # y_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(hadvice[2])]]) # y_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(y_lab, plot_width = 5) title <- paste0(x_lab) title_wrap <- wrap_titles(title) buffer <- mean(dat$p, na.rm = TRUE) / 4 ylim <- c(0, ceiling(max(dat$p, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer)) x_var <- names(dat)[1] (plot <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(1)) %>% mutate(!!sym(x_var) := map_chr(as.character(!!sym(x_var)), dynamic_str_wrap, plot_width = 7, num_labels = num_labels, char_width = 0.08, margin = 0.1)) %>% mutate(!!sym(x_var) := factor(!!sym(x_var), levels = unique(!!sym(x_var)))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(x_var), y = p)) + geom_col() + geom_text(aes(label = round(p, 1)), vjust = -1.5, size = 11, size.unit = "pt") + theme_gray() + labs(title = title_wrap, x = NULL, y = "%" ) + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) + theme( plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1), text = element_text(size = 11), # This seems to have no effect??? plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5), axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10), size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10), size = 11) )) if (!is_null(colour)) { if(colour == "pal") { plot <- plot + geom_col(aes(fill = !!sym(x_var))) + theme(legend.position = "none") if(!is_null(palette)) { if (palette %in% rownames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info)) { plot <- plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette = palette) } else { plot <- plot + scale_fill_manual(values = get(palette)) } } } else { plot <- plot + geom_col(fill = colour) } } return(plot) } bar(hadvice) bar(hadvice, colour = "pal") bar(hadvice, colour = "pal", palette = "Set2") bar(hadvice, colour = "pal", palette = "Accent") bar(hadvice, colour = "pal", palette = "ncl_oppo2") bar(hadvice, colour = "#7082d4") ```
**Step 4:** see if it works well with other variables... ```{r} bsa %>% freq(RAgecat5) %>% bar(colour = "pal") bsa %>% freq(RAgecat5) %>% bar(colour = "pal", palette = "Set2") bsa %>% freq(RAgecat5) %>% bar(colour = "pal", palette = "nbl") bsa %>% freq(RAgecat5) %>% bar(colour = "pal", palette = "npi") bsa %>% freq(RAgecat5) %>% bar(colour = "pal", palette = "YlGn") bsa %>% freq(RAgecat5) %>% bar(colour = "pal", palette = "OrRd") ```
### X by Y bar chart, labelling Y values ```{r} # Using the leftrigh table defined above... leftrigh leftrigh <- bsa %>% filter(!is.na(dolefidl)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = fct_drop(as_factor(dolefidl))) #### Set up ```{r, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE} library(tidyverse) library(ggpubr) data(mpg) ``` Every row in mpg is a car, every column a feature of that car. mpg stands for miles per gallon. ```{r} head(mpg) ```
## Basics of bar charts These uses the geom_col() function to display values *in* the data, geom_bar() to count the cases in a group. In this example, average highway miles per gallon (hwy) is displayed by a the type of car (class). ```{r} (hwy_class <- mpg %>% group_by(class) %>% summarise_at(vars(hwy), list(average_hwy= ~round(mean(.x), digits = 1)))) ```
### A basic bar chart That data is then fed to ggplot to produce a simple bar chart. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy)) ```
### A horizontal bar chart ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy)) + coord_flip() ```
## Amend fill colour
#### Standard gglot colours ```{r} plot <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, fill=class) + geom_col(width=0.5, colour = "black") + theme_minimal() plot ``` #### Other options ```{r} ggarrange( plot + scale_fill_grey() + theme(legend.position="none"), plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette="PuRd") + theme(legend.position="none"), plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette="Blues") + theme(legend.position="none"), ncol = 1, nrow = 3) ```
### Fill by another variable ```{r} (hwy_class_year <- mpg %>% group_by(class, year) %>% summarise_at(vars(hwy), list(average_hwy_year = ~round(mean(.x), 1)))) ```
The second variable is now the fill colour. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class_year, aes(x=class, y=average_hwy_year, fill=year)) + geom_col(width=0.5, colour="black") ```
The position argument (setting dodge2) moves the bars to appear alongside each other rather than stacked. ```{r} plot <- ggplot(data=hwy_class_year, aes(x=class, y=average_hwy_year, fill=year)) + geom_bar(stat="identity", position = "dodge2") plot ```
## Adding labels to data The geom_text function is what adds the labels: - had to move the aes() bit out of the geom_bar() bit to make this work.\ - the vjust bit moves it above and below the bar. A lower minus number would be higher above the bar. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy), vjust=-1) ```
Here the label is below the bar, vjust=1.5. The colour has been switched to white and the size increased also. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy), vjust=1.5, colour="white", size=6) ``` #### Adding them to our dodged plot above. We also have to 'dodge' the position of the labels within geom_text, again in the position argument. ```{r} plot + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy_year), vjust=1.6, color="white", position = position_dodge2(0.9), size=3.5) ```

## Other formatting
### Bar width Amend bar width within geom_col argument with 'width'. The default is 0.9, smaller values make bars smaller. Max = 1 and removes all space between bars. If you make the entire graph wider or narrower, the bar dimensions will scale proportionally. ```{r} more_space <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), width=0.9) less_space <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), width=0.5) ggarrange(more_space, less_space, ncol = 1) ```
### Change colours In the below the colour affects only the outline, without the fill the bars would be dark grey still. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), colour="blue", fill="white", width = 0.5) ```
Or bar colour can be changed by groups. - Add colour=var, where var is the variable you want to vary the colours by. ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, colour=class) + geom_col(fill="white", width=0.5) ```
### Apply themes ```{r} p <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), fill="steelblue") p + theme_minimal() ```
## Select categories to show You can also select which items to show: ```{r} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, label=average_hwy)) + scale_x_discrete(limits=c("suv", "minivan", "pickup")) ```
## Alternative statistics
#### Barplot of counts Similar to a histogram, the stat="bin" command allows ggplot() to work like table(), but specifically for *numeric* values. ```{r} ggplot(data=mpg) + aes(x=cyl) + geom_bar(stat="bin") ```
Or with *character* values, try geom_bar without an argument. ```{r} ggplot(data=mpg) + aes(x=class) + geom_bar() ```
